title: UV and LED curing lamps: manufacturer instructions and open questions
audience: Mobile nail technicians who use UV or LED lamps to cure gel or other nail products at client locations
learningOutcomes: Locate the manufacturer's instructions and the product's safety data sheet for each lamp and product in use
Describe the set-up and handling steps the manufacturer's instructions require for the lamp in use
State which UV and LED exposure duties are not yet confirmed for this course, and what must be done before relying on any limit
referencesAtStart: No official source on UV or LED lamp exposure has been read for this course. The sources for this lesson are the manufacturer's instructions for each lamp and the safety data sheet for each product. See officialReferences and the UNCONFIRMED notes below.

instruction.heading: What this lesson does and does not establish
instruction.body: Many nail services use a UV or LED lamp to cure a gel or similar product. This lesson explains how to find and follow the manufacturer's instructions for the lamp and the product. It does not set an exposure limit, a session length, a distance or a safe frequency, because no source for those has been read for this course. Where a figure appears on a manufacturer's sheet, the technician follows that sheet for that lamp and product, and records it. Any general statement about lamp exposure, such as a duty to protect the skin or eyes, must be taken from a confirmed source before it is written into the business's procedure. Until then it is marked UNCONFIRMED.

instruction.heading: Setting up for a lamp at a client's location
instruction.body: Before the lamp is switched on, the technician checks the lamp's manual for the power supply, the lamp type and the curing time the product manufacturer gives. The lamp is placed on a stable surface away from the client's bedding, clothing and water. Cables are kept clear of the work area so that they do not trip the technician or the client. The technician confirms that the lamp is the one approved for the products in the kit, and that its manual is held in the kit. Any lamp with a damaged housing, cable or switch is not used, and the technician records the fault and removes the lamp from service until it has been checked.

instruction.heading: Recording lamps and the questions still open
instruction.body: The business keeps a record of each lamp in use, with the make, model, the manual's location and the date of the last check. The record also notes the products the lamp is used with, and their safety data sheets. The following points are UNCONFIRMED for this course and must be resolved from a source before the business relies on them: whether UV and LED exposure from curing lamps is covered by any state or national duty that applies to a mobile nail business; what protection, if any, the client's eyes and skin need during curing; and whether any specific limit on exposure applies in any location the business visits. The business records the open questions in its procedure review, and does not present an answer to them to clients.

procedure: Locate the manufacturer's manual for the lamp and the safety data sheet for each product cured under it
Check the lamp for damage to the housing, cable and switch, and take out of service any lamp with a fault
Set up the lamp on a stable surface, clear of water, bedding and clothing, with the cable out of the work area
Follow the curing time and method the product manufacturer gives, and do not extend it without a sourced reason
Record the lamp, the product and the date of use on the visit record
Record any client concern about the lamp, and refer the question to the procedure review

workedExamples.situation: A technician is asked by a client whether the lamp is safe to use while she is pregnant.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the technician say, and what should be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: No source for this course states a safety position on lamp use in pregnancy, so the technician must not give a safety assurance or a warning as fact. The technician can say that the lamp is used as the manufacturer directs and that the business is checking its position. The technician records the question, refers it to the business owner, and offers the client a choice of service that does not use the lamp, if the business offers one on its approved list.

workedExamples.situation: A lamp's cable is cracked near the plug at a home visit, and the lamp still switches on.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the technician finish the visit with the lamp?
workedExamples.reasoning: A damaged cable is a fault, and the lamp is taken out of service. The technician does not use it, records the fault and the location, and completes the service without the lamp only if the service and its product can be finished that way under the approved procedure. Otherwise the service is rescheduled. The lamp is checked or replaced before its next use.

equipmentAndPpe: Manufacturer's manual for each lamp, held in the kit
Safety data sheet for each product cured under a lamp
Record of lamps in use, with the date of the last check
Eye and skin protection only where the manufacturer's instructions or the approved procedure require it

commonErrors.error: Extending the curing time to be sure the product is set.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the curing time the product manufacturer gives. Extending it has not been checked against a source for this course.

commonErrors.error: Using a lamp with a damaged cable because it still works.
commonErrors.prevention: Take any faulty lamp out of service, record the fault, and check it before it is used again.

commonErrors.error: Telling a client that lamp use is safe or unsafe, without a source.
commonErrors.prevention: Say that the business is checking its position, record the question, and refer it. Do not give a safety statement that is not sourced.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: UV and LED lamp exposure duties and limits: UNCONFIRMED for this course. No source has been read. Do not state a limit, a duty or a safe session length until it is sourced.
Follow the manufacturer's manual and the product's safety data sheet for the lamp and product in use. These are the only sources for specific curing times and set-up in this lesson.
Completing this lesson does not certify any technician to use a lamp, and does not satisfy any licence or training requirement that may apply to lamp use.

qualityStandard: Every lamp in use has a manual held in the kit and a record in the lamp register
Curing times follow the product manufacturer's instructions
Every open question on lamp exposure is recorded as UNCONFIRMED until sourced
documentationEvidence: Lamp register with make, model, manual location and last check date
Visit record showing the lamp and product used
Record of any client question or fault, and the review that followed
summary: The manufacturer's manual and the product's safety data sheet govern curing times and set-up
No exposure limit is stated in this course, because none has been sourced
A faulty lamp is taken out of service
Open questions on lamp exposure are recorded and referred, not answered from memory

knowledgeChecks.question: A lamp's cable is damaged but the lamp still switches on. What should the technician do?
options: Use the lamp, since it still works, and note the fault later
Take the lamp out of service, record the fault, and check it before further use
Wrap the cable in tape and continue the service

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should a technician find the curing time for a product used under a lamp?
options: From the product manufacturer's instructions, and not extended without a sourced reason
From a figure the technician remembers from another brand
By doubling the time for a safer result

referencesAtEnd: Official references, end of lesson: none read for UV or LED exposure in this course. Manufacturer manuals and product safety data sheets are the sources for set-up and curing times.
sourceReferences: Manufacturer's manual for each lamp: the source for set-up and handling. Held in the kit. Not a regulatory source
Product safety data sheet for each product cured under a lamp: the source for product hazards and controls
UV and LED lamp exposure duties, limits, eye and skin protection, and session length: UNCONFIRMED. No official source read for this course. Do not rely on this lesson for any limit
